profile.warning: Inclusive paths overlap. These are priority signals, not hard speedup limits or grounds to reject small gains.

diagnosis: Full PGO was repeatedly paid before performance screening.
Unrelated speculative components accumulated and made negative package results hard to attribute.
Read-hit counts were not performance evidence.
Background load fitting does not stabilize CPU time/frequency across sessions; identical baseline wall throughput changed substantially.
Current loop edits address a limited fraction of samples; trigger/effect/damage processing deserves primary attention.
decision: Finish the already-built candidate using one predeclared24-pair comparison, with no new implementation or additional PGO.
If positive, run2604+one24 throughput+one24 calibration and review before deployment. If negative, retain/reject this combination without adding unrelated changes or repeating until positive.
Then prioritize one equivalent weapon-trigger/damage chain. Use actual baseline DLL as the functional oracle and local performance screening before the expensive full build.
Keep small inconclusive changes in the ledger. Compose them only with a specific shared-hot-path or interaction hypothesis; do not require each edit to be independently significant.
Keep paired main-thread CPU and wall time as causal evidence. Report contemporaneous baseline conditions separately from20%-load fitted absolute throughput.
Defer the member-pointer-table and allocator/variant proposals while evaluating the larger trigger/effect chain.
